name: Halden
positioning: Fictional camera maker. The Halden R is a mechanical rangefinder camera built to be used for decades and repaired, not replaced. Used to study the structure of a hardware product page.
audience: Photographers choosing a film camera they will carry every day and keep for years.
voice: Specs in plain numbers: millimetres, grams, fractions of a second
Talk about use and wear, never about perfection

direction.concept: Worn in. Never worn out. The camera is shown with its real wear, and the page treats each mark as proof that it keeps working.
direction.tier: Cinematic hardware page. Structure studied from Apple product pages (black product hero, highlights, product viewer, story sections, light specs close), measured for layout only. No Apple media, copy, fonts, icons or code. The 3D model is Poly Haven's Camera 01 (CC0).
devices: One camera travels the whole page: a pinned 3D stage turns, closes in and comes apart as you scroll
Engraved numbers: specs set in small uppercase mono like the markings on a lens ring
Brass appears only where metal shows through the paint: the one action and the engraved markings
invariants: One camera model with its real wear, never retouched to look new
Black stage for the product, warm grey for reading
Geist for words, Geist Mono for engraved numbers
Every spec is fictional and the footer says so
variables: Which part the camera turns toward
How far apart the parts come

imagery.subject: One rangefinder camera with a leather strap, worn at the edges, rendered in 3D on a black stage
imagery.materials: Black paint over brass, chrome, glass, leather
imagery.lighting: A small photo studio: soft key light from above left and a clean reflection on the lens
imagery.palette: Black #000000, warm grey #f4f3f0, brass #d8b46a on the dark stage
invariants: The same model and finish everywhere
Source and licence recorded in source-3d/PROVENANCE.md
avoid: Apple product photos, renders, icons or copy
Real camera brand names or logos on the model
Models or textures without a CC0 or public-domain licence

motion.character: The camera starts from the back, turns to face you as the title arrives, then the lens and strap come away from the body so each part can be named. Later sections move the same camera toward the part they describe. Drag to turn it in the closer look.
motion.reducedMotion: Each section shows the camera at rest in its final pose; poses change as cuts. No idle drift. Dragging still works.
